Senses.Explanation: As a closing formula, take care dismisses an assembly or participant at the end of an address or encounter. The exact rows retain their separate speakers, narrators, participants, and quoted layers; no single deployment is made to resolve all others.

Occurrences.Kwic: 屢承翰教，珍重法門，筆舌難盡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan (破山禪師語錄), Poshan Haiming's reply-letter to academy chancellor Tan Sao'an. Poshan Haiming is the exact author, thanking his correspondent for repeated written instruction and for treating the teaching gate with care.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又能珍重此錄，廣為流佈
Occurrences.AttributionNote: an unnamed Chan practitioner from Jiahe is the exact actor. Drafts from Chan Master Weilin Daopei's Traveling Hermitage (為霖禪師旅泊菴稿), Weilin Daopei's preface to Daqian's recorded sayings. The exact grammatical actor is the Chan practitioner identified only as being from Jiahe: Weilin says that this practitioner had long trained under the hammer and whisk, cherished the record, and spread it widely. All six rungs supply no personal name for him.

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: an unnamed Chan practitioner from Jiahe
ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The full passage assigns the stored wording to the reviewed textual actor.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若欲珍重其事，且放過諸人一著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Record of Chan Master Juelang Sheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄), New Year's Eve informal address. Juelang Daosheng is the exact speaker of the stored counsel that, if his listeners wish to treat the matter with due care, he will first let them off one move.

Senses.Explanation: To treasure or preserve actively describes valuing a teaching, record, or matter and keeping it in circulation; this differs from the dismissal formula. The exact rows retain their separate speakers, narrators, participants, and quoted layers; no single deployment is made to resolve all others.

Senses.Explanation: Ācārya is a title or direct form of address for a monastic instructor; in ordination compounds it can designate the office-holder who performs a defined ceremonial role. In encounters the title is often spoken directly to the person being questioned or answered. The bare title does not by itself decide rank, lineage, or ordination office.
